required_fixes: Restore historical member-level failure precedence in the refactored serial Phase 2 path. The old _finish_population_step checked MAX_PROPAGULES_PER_STEP immediately after each member's _advance_individual() result, before advancing the next member. Current _advance_units_serial first runs _advance_unit_worker() over the whole workset and only afterwards applies the propagule limit, so a later member failure can mask an earlier canonical A5_PROPAGULE_LIMIT.

Make parallel advance return/interpret per-member outcomes (or an equivalent structure) in canonical member order so the main thread can interleave each member's semantic failure and propagule-limit check exactly as the accepted serial path did. Add a focused falsifier where an earlier member causes propagule overflow and a later member in the same workset fails; serial reference and parallel advance must both return the same earlier A5_PROPAGULE_LIMIT.

findings.summary: Whole-workset advance aggregation changes canonical failure precedence.
evidence: Accepted main processes each member as: _advance_individual -> append that member -> enforce MAX_PROPAGULES_PER_STEP -> then move to the next member.

Reviewed HEAD c12f6ead changes serial Phase 2 to _advance_unit_worker(task_entries...) for the entire workset, where any later member failure returns immediately before _advance_units_serial sees propagules from earlier successful members.

The parallel path has the same aggregation boundary: _advance_unit_worker returns one success/failure dictionary for the whole workset, and main-thread canonical merge performs the propagule limit only after the worker reports overall success.

Therefore an earlier member that would canonically trigger A5_PROPAGULE_LIMIT can be masked by a later member failure inside the same workset. This violates the Work Order claim that failures are consumed in canonical workset/member order and also changes the pre-existing serial path.
findings.required_disposition: Repair the aggregation boundary so member results are interpreted canonically one member at a time; preserve no-shared-state worker execution.

evidence_gaps: The 136-check Parallel Advance suite does not contain a mixed same-workset falsifier that forces propagule-limit overflow before a later member-level advance failure.

post_build_critique.unnecessary_complexity: The two-phase bounded Thread-wave design remains auditable and appropriately explicit for this checkpoint.
post_build_critique.duplicate_truth: None observed in canonical state; worker data and scheduler telemetry remain execution-only.
post_build_critique.implicit_owner: None. Field allocation remains A4-owned; A5 owns lifecycle transition; Runtime composes but does not acquire allocator ownership.
post_build_critique.coupling_reduction: The shared allocation helper is a good refactor, but serial and parallel Phase 2 must share a member-level canonical interpretation contract rather than a whole-workset success/failure aggregate.
post_build_critique.design_regression: Yes, limited to error precedence around global propagule admission limit versus later member failures within the same workset.
post_build_critique.recommended_repair: Have workers compute isolated per-member outcomes, then let the main thread consume those outcomes member-by-member in canonical order, applying A5_PROPAGULE_LIMIT after each successful member before considering the next member's outcome. Keep the serial reference member-by-member as the oracle.

risk_assessment: MEDIUM with one blocking deterministic semantics regression. Successful-state byte/hash equivalence is strongly covered and current Windows/portable execution is green, but acceptance requires exact failure behavior as well. The current workset-level result aggregation can reorder which canonical error wins without changing successful-state bytes, so the existing green equivalence tests do not falsify this edge case.
summary: Fresh exact-head review found one blocking failure-precedence defect. The concurrency architecture and canonical-state isolation are otherwise sound. Repair must restore member-level canonical interpretation around A5_PROPAGULE_LIMIT and add a same-workset mixed-failure falsifier before a fresh review can PASS.
